claim_text: Approximately 75% of service members self-report taking at least one dietary supplement at least once a week.

evidence.text: Overall, 74% reported using ≥1 DS/wk.

Editorial summary of the study abstract: DS means dietary supplements. This cross-sectional study surveyed personnel from the US Air Force, Army, Marine Corps and Navy. Between December 2018 and August 2019, 26,681 service members completed questionnaires, about 18% of those successfully contacted. Supplement use was self-reported; the reported 74% is a survey estimate, not a census of every service member.

claim_text: Dietary supplement use has documented adverse events and positive drug tests.

evidence.text: Editorial summary of the study abstract: In a questionnaire study of US military personnel conducted in 2018–2019, 18% of supplement users taking products at least weekly reported one or more associated adverse effects. These were self-reports in a cross-sectional study rather than proof that each supplement caused the reported event.

Editorial summary of FDA questions 1 and 5: Laboratory testing found undeclared drugs and chemicals in selected products marketed for weight loss. Identified ingredients included fenproporex. FDA describes fenproporex as an amphetamine derivative that could produce a positive amphetamine urinalysis. The page also describes serious potential adverse effects of stimulants.

Editorial summary: OPSS receives questions about whether bodybuilding, testosterone-boosting and weight-loss supplements could lead to a positive military drug test. It explains that laboratory testing is needed to determine whether a product contains undeclared drugs or controlled substances.

claim_text: Half of body weight in pounds, expressed as fluid ounces of water per day, is generally a good starting point for hydration.

evidence.text: Daily water intake recommendations vary by age, sex, pregnancy status, activity level, and breastfeeding status.

Editorial summary: CDC explains that water intake comes from plain water, other beverages and foods. More water may be needed in hot climates, during greater physical activity, fever, diarrhea or vomiting. This page does not give a formula of half body weight in pounds as fluid ounces of plain water per day.

claim_text: Behavioral health consultants can provide brief behavioral treatment for insomnia.

evidence.text: Editorial summary of the 2020 patient guide: Cognitive behavioral therapy for insomnia (CBT-I) and brief behavioral therapy for insomnia (BBT-I) are specialized behavioral treatments for chronic insomnia. Treatment is available in primary care, behavioral health and sleep clinics. Patients may receive these treatments from specially trained clinical psychologists or social workers, depending on the facility.

Editorial summary: BBT-I treats insomnia by addressing sleep-specific behaviors through multiple sessions. Its components include sleep restriction, stimulus control and some sleep hygiene. Certain coexisting conditions can require tailoring or delaying treatment.

evidence.text: Changes in your schedule or environment can cause or raise your risk of insomnia.

Editorial summary: NHLBI lists shift or night work as factors that can disturb the sleep-wake cycle. Frequently changing the normal routine, including sleep schedule, is also listed as a lifestyle risk factor for sleep problems.

claim_text: Following the executive order, the Marine Corps established a COVID-19 reinstatement cell and a pathway for eligible Marines to return to service.

evidence.text: Source summary: Executive Order 14184 was signed January 27, 2025. Subsequent guidance established return-to-service and records-correction processes for people affected by the vaccine mandate. The Marine Corps implemented a program involving recruiters and the COVID Reinstatement Cell. Applicants submit information so staff can assess their circumstances and explain a pathway.

Source summary: The return-to-service process includes review of individual circumstances, required medical and administrative screening, and eligibility and outcome decisions made case by case under governing policy. Submitting an application does not oblige an applicant to return to service.

claim_text: The 2026 SoSNIE was the seventh iteration of the annual experiment.

evidence.text: Source summary of the April 8, 2026 article and March 18 photo captions: NIWC Atlantic describes the 2026 SoSNIE as the seventh annual experiment. Joint forces and engineers tested end-to-end mission threads and emerging technologies. The experiment involved more than 40 communications technologies and more than 150 participants from military services, government and industry.

Source summary of the March 26, 2025 article: The annual SoSNIE held in 2025 is described as the seventh year the command hosted the event. The article reports approximately 45 systems and approximately 240 active participants and attendees. It says the team hoped to continue its growth into 2026.
